newsitem.title: UK: Oil prices steady as traders take profits.
newsitem.headline: Oil prices steady as traders take profits.

text.p: Oil prices ended almost unchanged on Monday after profit-taking wiped out earlier gains on a refinery problem in the United States.

Traders in the United States suspected a problem at Amoco's Texas City refinery after the company bought as much as 300,000 barrels of gasoline on the spot market, presumably to cover lost output. A government regulator then confirmed a valve fault at the Texas plant.
Gasoline on the U.S. spot market rose a healthy two cents a gallon, which pulled up the crude oil market on both sides of the Atlantic.
But after a 50 cent rally in the middle of the day, benchmark North Sea Brent crude futures for December delivery closed six cents down at $24.16 a barrel.
Low stocks in the United States were seen as the reason for the market's sensitivity to any supply disruption.
"Inventories are extremely low," said consultant Gary Ross of the Petroleum Industry Research Associates. "The market is very vulnerable to surprises because there is no cushion."
Prices may rise even further before the end of the year, Ross told an industry conference in London.
